You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.
  - Grab ↔ a ride-hailing marketplace: true.
  - Grab ↔ a traditional car-rental operator with no on-demand marketplace: false.
  - Rippling ↔ a smaller HRIS/payroll platform: true.
  - Rippling ↔ device-security software for mobile workers: false.
  - Brex ↔ a corporate-card and spend-management platform: true.
  - Brex ↔ consumer personal-finance budgeting software: false.
  - OpenAI ↔ a foundation-model/API company: true.
  - OpenAI ↔ a consultancy that implements AI tools for clients: false.
  - Datadog ↔ an application-performance-monitoring and observability platform: true.
  - Datadog ↔ a generic IT consulting firm: false.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ an endpoint-security platform: true.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ a general-purpose IT monitoring tool with no security product: false.
  - Procore ↔ construction project-management software: true.
  - Procore ↔ a construction contractor: false.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ field-service management software for trades businesses: true.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ a plumbing company that uses field-service software: false.
  - Teladoc ↔ a virtual-care/telehealth platform: true.
  - Teladoc ↔ a health-insurance carrier with no telehealth product: false.
  - Veeva ↔ life-sciences CRM or clinical-operations software: true.
  - Veeva ↔ a generic CRM with no life-sciences focus: false.

The problem we're solving is simple: most meeting decisions don't result in action. Not because people don't care — but because the gap between "we decided this" and "this is now done" is filled with friction. Manual copy-paste, app-switching, forgotten follow-ups.

Geniffy removes that friction. The meeting ends, the work begins — automatically, accurately, with you in control at every step.

---

We're a small founding team building fast. Right now we're deep in the product — live transcription, real-time execution into your apps, a team workspace, and a follow-through engine that tracks whether commitments from meetings actually get done.

This is early and we know it. But the direction is clear and we're moving.

Contextual AI: Ask complex questions about your architecture, history, or specific lines of code in natural language and get instant, cited answers.

Zero Knowledge Loss: Every decision and change is indexed. New hires can onboard in days, not months, by "chatting" with the project's entire history.

Automated Documentation: Stop writing stale docs. ProjIntel.ai keeps your understanding of the system real-time and accurate.

🔗 Powerful Integrations: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Jira, Trello, Asana, and Notion.

Build faster with the context you need, exactly when you need it.

You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.
  - Grab ↔ a ride-hailing marketplace: true.
  - Grab ↔ a traditional car-rental operator with no on-demand marketplace: false.
  - Rippling ↔ a smaller HRIS/payroll platform: true.
  - Rippling ↔ device-security software for mobile workers: false.
  - Brex ↔ a corporate-card and spend-management platform: true.
  - Brex ↔ consumer personal-finance budgeting software: false.
  - OpenAI ↔ a foundation-model/API company: true.
  - OpenAI ↔ a consultancy that implements AI tools for clients: false.
  - Datadog ↔ an application-performance-monitoring and observability platform: true.
  - Datadog ↔ a generic IT consulting firm: false.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ an endpoint-security platform: true.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ a general-purpose IT monitoring tool with no security product: false.
  - Procore ↔ construction project-management software: true.
  - Procore ↔ a construction contractor: false.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ field-service management software for trades businesses: true.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ a plumbing company that uses field-service software: false.
  - Teladoc ↔ a virtual-care/telehealth platform: true.
  - Teladoc ↔ a health-insurance carrier with no telehealth product: false.
  - Veeva ↔ life-sciences CRM or clinical-operations software: true.
  - Veeva ↔ a generic CRM with no life-sciences focus: false.

B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).

    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.

properties.name: TejDocs
properties.description:
TejDocs is a secure document sharing and data room platform built for businesses that handle sensitive information.

Most teams still rely on email, WhatsApp, or shared drives to exchange confidential files—leaving no control, no visibility, and no way to prevent data leaks. TejDocs fixes this by putting access, tracking, and accountability at the center of document sharing.

With TejDocs, you can share documents using secure links instead of attachments. Access can be restricted by email, IP address, device, or time. Every file can carry dynamic watermarks showing viewer identity, and every activity—view, download, or access attempt—is logged in a complete audit trail.

TejDocs also includes virtual data room capabilities for structured document sharing during audits, fundraising, legal reviews, vendor onboarding, and compliance processes. You can organize files into folders, invite internal or external users, assign granular permissions, and revoke access instantly—without resending files.

Built in India by Serverstock, TejDocs is designed for Indian businesses with a strong focus on data protection, operational control, and regulatory readiness. The platform aligns with Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act requirements and follows industry best practices for encryption and access security.

TejDocs is ideal for legal firms, finance teams, manufacturing companies, startups, and service providers who need to share confidential documents without losing control.

Ranck Asset Brokerage (RAB) helps solve the drain distressed assets have on a bank's balance sheet and on their employees who put out these fires everyday. 

Using a marketing plan that takes advantage of RAB's buyer network, coupled with advertising strategies on platforms like Facebook, LinkedIn, WSJ, Loopnet and Craigslist, banks find themselves with qualified buyers who finish due diligence and get purchase agreements signed and closed quickly, at release prices banks find satisfactory. 

If you are in charge of your bank's special assets/workout division, or if you can put me in contact with one of your colleagues who is, I would love to speak to you about your specific situation and see if we can do business together and get these bad loans off your books. 

RAB also cultivates relationships with note buyers, hedge funds, and asset companies who are always on the lookout for fresh deals sourced direct from institutional sellers, ie banks and credit unions. If you're one of these note buyers, what is of upmost importance for me when we connect with one another is learning about what has worked well for you in the past, and then supplying you with more of these types of deals in the future. 

I have a continuously growing database of over 200 banks, and each bank has a greater than average presence of non-preforming loans on their books (which makes them a great opportunity for lucrative deals). I deal in the most popular asset classes: single-family residential first and junior liens, multifamily notes, CRE notes (both owner occupied and not), commercial and residential construction, and farmland. 

If you are a note buyer who is looking for notes, please do not be hesitant to contact me. I would love to hear about your previous successes, which asset type(s) you are targeting, what states you deal in, and what your plans are for the future.

entity.name: TejDocs

TejDocs is a secure document sharing and data room platform built for businesses that handle sensitive information.

Most teams still rely on email, WhatsApp, or shared drives to exchange confidential files—leaving no control, no visibility, and no way to prevent data leaks. TejDocs fixes this by putting access, tracking, and accountability at the center of document sharing.

With TejDocs, you can share documents using secure links instead of attachments. Access can be restricted by email, IP address, device, or time. Every file can carry dynamic watermarks showing viewer identity, and every activity—view, download, or access attempt—is logged in a complete audit trail.

TejDocs also includes virtual data room capabilities for structured document sharing during audits, fundraising, legal reviews, vendor onboarding, and compliance processes. You can organize files into folders, invite internal or external users, assign granular permissions, and revoke access instantly—without resending files.

Built in India by Serverstock, TejDocs is designed for Indian businesses with a strong focus on data protection, operational control, and regulatory readiness. The platform aligns with Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act requirements and follows industry best practices for encryption and access security.

TejDocs is ideal for legal firms, finance teams, manufacturing companies, startups, and service providers who need to share confidential documents without losing control.

You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
